chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no problem with the man who marries by Mut'a with the woman upon his decision, but there is no alternative for him from giving her something, because if there was to occur an event with him (of death), there would not happen to be any inheritance for her.
ai.seo_question: What is the requirement for inheritance in temporary marriage according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial rights within temporary marriage (Mut'a), emphasizing that while the man retains discretion over the terms, he must provide a specific gift or portion to secure the woman's inheritance rights upon his death. This ruling underscores the contractual nature of Mut'a in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from permanent marriage by linking the woman's financial security directly to the husband's estate rather than automatic statutory shares.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umehyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is no problem with the man who marries by Mut’a with the woman upon his decision, but there is no alternative for him from giving her something, because if there was to occur an event with him (of death), there would not happen to be any inheritance for her’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is not unlawful for a man to marry a woman in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) because of leaving herself at his disposal, but it is necessary to give her something; if anything happens to him she will not inherit his legacy.’”
